content.text: Hi — I'm doing well, thanks! How can I help you today?
give me all samples of markdown

Do you mean examples of Markdown syntax (how to write headings, lists, code, tables, etc.)? Below is a comprehensive set of commonly used Markdown samples (core CommonMark + common extensions like GitHub Flavored Markdown). For each feature I show the Markdown source (in a code block) and a one-line note about how it renders. Note that different platforms/renderers may support slightly different extensions (e.g., footnotes, definition lists, math). Basic text and headings ``` # H1 ## H2 ### H3 This is a paragraph. (two spaces at end creates a line break) This is the next line of the same paragraph. ``` Renders: Headings H1/H2/H3 and a paragraph with a line break. Emphasis ``` *italic* _italic_ **bold** __bold__ ***bold italic*** ~~strikethrough~~ ``` Renders: italic, bold, bold italic, strikethrough (GFM). Inline code and code blocks ``` Inline code: `const x = 1;` Fenced code block with language: ```js function hello() { console.log("Hello"); } ``` Indented code block: line one line two ``` Renders: inline code and syntax-highlighted fenced code block (if renderer supports language), and indented code block. Blockquotes ``` > This is a blockquote. > > > Nested quote. > > Quote with paragraph and list: > > - item 1 > - item 2 ``` Renders: quoted text and nested blockquote and list inside quote. Lists ``` Unordered: - Item A - Item B - Nested item B1 Ordered: 1. First 2. Second 1. Sub-first Mixed: 1. First - Second (still allowed by many renderers) ``` Renders: ordered/unordered lists and nesting. Links and autolinks ``` Inline link: [OpenAI](https://openai.com) Reference-style: [Google][g] [g]: https://google.com "Google home" Autolink: ``` Renders: clickable links; autolink automatically becomes link. Images ``` Inline image: ![Alt text](https://example.com/image.png "Optional title") Reference-style image: ![Logo][logo] [logo]: https://example.com/logo.png ``` Renders: images with alt text and optional title. Tables (GFM / Common extensions) ``` | Name | Age | City | |-------|-----:|-----------| | Alice | 30 | New York | | Bob | 25 | San Francisco | ``` Renders: a table with alignment (right align Age). Task lists (GFM) ``` - [ ] Task one - [x] Task done ``` Renders: checkbox list (interactive checkboxes on some platforms). Footnotes (Pandoc/GFM-like renderers) ``` Here is a statement.[^1] [^1]: This is the footnote text. ``` Renders: footnote reference and note (not supported by all renderers). Definition lists (Pandoc) ``` Term 1 : Definition one Term 2 : Definition two line 1 : Definition two line 2 ``` Renders: definition list (supported by some renderers like Pandoc). Horizontal rule ``` --- *** ___ ``` Renders: horizontal divider. Inline HTML and raw HTML blocks ``` This is raw HTML inline.
HTML block is allowed in Markdown (renderer permitting).
``` Renders: raw HTML if the renderer allows it (sanitization may remove some tags). Escaping characters ``` To show a literal asterisk: \* Backslash escapes let you show characters like \*, \`, \_, \{ \}, etc. ``` Renders: shows literal Markdown characters. Emojis (GFM) ``` I love markdown! :sparkles: :heart: ``` Renders: emoji shortcodes to emoji (if platform supports). Mentions and issues (GFM) ``` Ping a user: @username Reference issue: #123 ``` Renders: platform-specific mention/issue links on systems like GitHub. YAML front matter (static site generators) ``` --- title: "My Post" date: 2026-02-01 tags: [markdown, example] --- # Post Title ``` Renders: front matter is metadata for processors (not shown in HTML content). Math (LaTeX) — renderer dependent (MathJax/Katex) ``` Inline: Euler's identity $e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0$. Display: $$ \int_{0}^{1} x^2 dx = \frac{1}{3} $$ ``` Renders: math when the renderer supports MathJax/Katex. Definition of code + language identifiers (fenced) ``` ```python def add(a, b): return a + b ``` ``` Renders: syntax-highlighted Python if supported. Diff or patch blocks (some renderers) ``` ```diff + added line - removed line ``` ``` Renders: colored diff style. Collapsible details (HTML) ```
Click to expand Hidden content here, including lists, code, etc.
``` Renders: collapsible section on supporting platforms. Advanced: nested constructs example ``` > ### Blockquote heading > - list item 1 > - list item 2 > > ```js > // code inside blockquote > console.log('inside quote'); > ``` ``` Renders: blockquote containing heading, list, and fenced code block. Escaping a code fence ``` If you need to show a fenced block in Markdown, you can fence it with more backticks: ````markdown ```js console.log("not executed"); ``` ```` ``` Renders: shows the fenced code block literally. Special characters and HTML entities ``` Use & for & and < for < when needed. ``` Renders: HTML entities. Notes on flavors and support - CommonMark is the standardized core spec (headings, emphasis, lists, code, blockquotes, links, images). - GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) adds tables, task lists, strikethrough, autolinks, and some other conveniences. - Pandoc/Markdown processors add footnotes, definition lists, citations, math, and more. - Static site generators and platforms may add front matter (YAML/TOML), special shortcodes, or sanitize HTML. If you want: - A single-file cheatsheet PDF or printable reference. - Examples in a specific flavor (GitHub, CommonMark, Pandoc, Markdown-it). - A rendered preview of any of the above examples. Tell me which format or flavor you prefer and I can produce a focused cheatsheet or a printable file.
